question: If a train 130 m long takes 6(1)/(2) seconds to cross a man who is walking at 12 km/h in the same direction in which the train going, then the speed of the train (in km/h) is:
solution:
Given:

A train 130 m long takes 6(1)/(2) seconds to cross a man who is walking at 12 km/h in the same direction in which the train going.

Formula used:

Distance = speed × time

Concept used:

Relative speed for Same direction = difference of their speed given

Calculation:

The train takes 6.5 sec to cross 130 m

So Relative speed will be 130/6.5 = 20 m/s

So Relative speed is 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h

The speed of the train will be 72 +12 = 84 km/h

**∴ The correct option is 1**
